t.1.80.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa, best of kings, filled with delight, enjoyed the pleasures he loved with the youth of Pūru.
t.1.80.3: He gratified the gods with sacrifices, and likewise the ancestors with śrāddha offerings, the wretched with acts of kindness, and the best of the twice-born with the desires they wished for.
t.1.80.2: As he desired, as his vigor allowed, as the time suited, and as it pleased him, that lord of kings enjoyed pleasures not opposed to dharma, just as befitted him alone.
t.1.80.5: And Yayāti protected all his subjects with righteousness, gladdening them as was fitting, like a second Indra in visible form.
t.1.80.4: He honored guests with food and drink, the Vaiśyas with protection, the Śūdras with kindness, and the Dasyus with firm restraint.
t.1.80.6: That king, valorous as a lion, young and given to the pleasures of the senses, enjoyed the highest happiness without transgressing dharma.
t.1.80.7: Having obtained the auspicious pleasures he desired, that king, the lord of men, sated and yet weary, remembered that the term of a thousand years was at its end.
t.1.80.8: The mighty one, knower of time, having reckoned the kalās and kāṣṭhās and judging that the time was then complete, spoke to his son Pūru.
t.1.80.9: As I desired, as my vigor allowed, and as the seasons permitted, O tamer of foes, I have enjoyed the objects of the senses with your youth, my son.
t.1.80.10: Pūru, I am pleased with you; blessings upon you! Take back this youth of yours, and take this kingdom as well, for you are the son who has done what is dear to me.
t.1.80.11: Then King Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, took back his old age, and Pūru once again received his own youth.
t.1.80.13: How, O lord, will you pass over Yadu, the eldest, the grandson of Śukra and son of Devayānī, and give the kingdom to Pūru?
t.1.80.12: When the king wished to consecrate Pūru, his youngest son, the social classes headed by the brāhmaṇas spoke these words to him.
t.1.80.14: Yadu was born as your eldest son, and after him Turvasu; Śarmiṣṭhā's son was Druhyu, and then Anu and Pūru as well.
t.1.80.15: How can a younger son, passing over his elder brothers, deserve the kingdom? This we bring to your attention; uphold the dharma.
t.1.80.16: Yayāti said: Let all the classes, with the brāhmaṇas at their head, hear my words as to why the kingdom must by no means be given by me to my eldest son.
t.1.80.17: My command was not obeyed by Yadu, my eldest son; and one who is hostile to his father is not regarded by the good as a true son.
t.1.80.18: The son who carries out the word of his mother and father, who is devoted to their welfare and does what is good for them, and who conducts himself toward his father and mother as a true son should, he alone is a son.
t.1.80.19: I have been disregarded by Yadu, and likewise by Turvasu too; and by Druhyu and by Anu as well, great contempt has been shown toward me.
t.1.80.20: Pūru has carried out my word, and I have been especially honored by him; my youngest heir is the one by whom my old age was borne. That desire of mine was fulfilled by Pūru, who acted in the true form of a son.
t.1.80.21: A boon was also granted by Śukra, Kāvya Uśanas himself: "The son who follows you shall be king, lord of the earth." Thus I entreat you, sirs: let Pūru be consecrated in the kingship.
t.1.80.22: The son who is endowed with virtues and always devoted to the welfare of his mother and father deserves every good fortune, O lord, even though he is the younger.
t.1.80.24: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed then by the contented townsfolk and country people, Nāhuṣa thereupon consecrated Pūru, his own begotten son, in his kingdom.
t.1.80.23: Pūru, the son who has done what is dear to you, is worthy of this kingdom; because of Śukra's granting of a boon, no answer can be spoken against it.
t.1.80.25: Having given the kingdom to Pūru and consecrated himself for dwelling in the forest, the king went forth from the city together with brahmins and ascetics.
t.1.80.26: From Yadu were born the Yādavas, and the sons of Turvasu are the Yavanas; the sons of Druhyu are the Bhojas, while from Anu come the Mleccha peoples.
t.1.80.27: But from Pūru comes the Paurava lineage, in which you were born, O king; and he, the self-controlled one, was to have this kingdom ruled for a thousand years.
